scope: Real browser, own temporary SQLite/local storage, real auth/refresh/client/worker/PDF/logo/export APIs; invalid access simulates an expired access challenge but temporal expiry is not claimed. Held deliveries retain real HTTP responses; only the specifically named first PDF401 is fabricated.
checks: A real invalid-access PUT401 triggers one real signed refresh rotation and a successful same-owner replay
Three simultaneous real HTTP401 reads share one real refresh and all finish under the original account
An actual old PUT401 delivered after another real login cannot start refresh, resend its DTO, or mutate the persisted previous-account client
A real successful old refresh response held across account replacement cannot overwrite the new token pair or retry the old read
A real rejected refresh401 delivered after account replacement preserves the new credentials and resolves the old operation
A real successful old-scope JSON response is discarded after account replacement
Logo GET and multipart POST both survive actual HTTP401 through the same real refresh coordinator and retain valid private-object behavior
A specifically fabricated first PDF401 triggers real refresh and an exact authorized PDF download from the real newly published plan
Personal-export helper remains authenticated and returns the current account after a real access401/refresh cycle
